knowledge_point.title: Determining the Equation of a Normal Line to a Curve at a Point

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2 x^{2} + 2 x + 1$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=4 x + 2
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(-1\right)=4 \left(-1\right) + 2=-2
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(-2\right)}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(1\right)&=\frac{1}{2}\left(x-\left(-1\right)\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{2}+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+\left(1\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{2} + \frac{3}{2}\\
\left(-2\right)y&=-x+\left(-1\right)+\left(-2\right)\\
x+\left(-2\right)y&=-3
\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient is $-2$ and the constant is $-3$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=x^{2} + x + 2$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=2 x + 1
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(-1\right)=2 \left(-1\right) + 1=-1
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(-1\right)}=1.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(2\right)&=1\left(x-\left(-1\right)\right)\\
y&=x+\left(1\right)+\left(2\right)\\
y&=x + 3\\
\left(-1\right)y&=-x+\left(-1\right)+\left(-2\right)\\
x+\left(-1\right)y&=-3
\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient is $-1$ and the constant is $-3$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2 x^{2} + x - 1$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=4 x + 1
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(2\right)=4 \left(2\right) + 1=9
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(9\right)}=- \frac{1}{9}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(9\right)&=- \frac{1}{9}\left(x-\left(2\right)\right)\\
y&=- \frac{x}{9}+\left(\frac{2}{9}\right)+\left(9\right)\\

\left(9\right)y&=-x+\left(2\right)+\left(81\right)\\
x+\left(9\right)y&=83
\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient is $9$ and the constant is $83$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=\frac{x^{6}}{8} - x^{3} + 1$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=\frac{3 x^{5}}{4} - 3 x^{2}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(2\right)=\frac{3 \left(2\right)^{5}}{4} - 3 \left(2\right)^{2}=12
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(12\right)}=- \frac{1}{12}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(1\right)&=- \frac{1}{12}\left(x-\left(2\right)\right)\\
y&=- \frac{x}{12}+\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)+\left(1\right)\\
y&=\frac{7}{6} - \frac{x}{12}\\
\left(12\right)y&=-x+\left(2\right)+\left(12\right)\\
x+\left(12\right)y&=14
\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient is $12$ and the constant is $14$.

$$

$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(14\right)}=- \frac{1}{14}.
$$

$$

x+\left(14\right)y&=142
\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient is $14$ and the constant is $142$.
